opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, the supply chain and the back office.

follow100Note: Walmart keeps just $3.00 of every $100 — about the thinnest margin on this site — but on $177.8B of quarterly revenue, $3.00 a hundred adds up to $5.3B. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $5,330M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $5,490M, of which $160M belongs to noncontrolling interests.
oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses swung from a $597M loss a year ago to a $275M gain — mostly fair-value moves on equity investments. Adjusted EPS of $0.66 excludes a $0.02 net gain from these items.
Higher fuel costs in distribution and fulfillment cut operating-income growth by roughly 250 basis points (in the company's adjusted framing).
otherDetail: Interest of $620M, net, partly offset by a $275M gain on equity and other investments — a year ago that investments line was a $597M loss.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: The big U.S. stores — net sales up 4.5%, comparable sales up 4.1%, with eCommerce growing strongly.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and e-commerce outside the U.S., including Flipkart in India — net sales up 18.0%.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: The warehouse-club business — net sales up 6.1%, or 3.9% excluding fuel.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Sam's Club membership fees plus advertising (Walmart Connect) and other income — the fastest-growing slice.

takeaways.text: Online sales grew 26% globally, U.S. comparable sales rose 4.1%, and International net sales jumped 18.0% — growth is coming from every segment at once.
takeaways.title: eCommerce is the growth engine

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 5.0% to $7.5B against 7.3% revenue growth — higher fuel costs in distribution and fulfillment took roughly 2.5 points off operating-income growth.
takeaways.title: Profit grew slower than sales

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS rose 19.6% to $0.67, helped by a $275M gain on equity investments versus a $597M loss a year ago. Adjusted EPS, which strips that out, was $0.66.
takeaways.title: EPS jumped on investment swings

verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 7.3% to $177.8B as eCommerce grew 26% — and with investment gains replacing last year's losses, profit attributable to Walmart rose 19% to $5.3B.
